previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and a history of steal syndrome was admitted from his extended care facility due to fatigue and malaise after missing a dialysis session. He presented with hyperkalemia and fluid overload, confirmed by elevated potassium and pulmonary edema on chest X-ray. He received timely hemodialysis, which improved his electrolytes and respiratory status. During the admission, he experienced narcotic-induced encephalopathy, which resolved after dose reduction. Pain management was optimized with palliative care input, transitioning to once-daily OxyContin and lower PRN oxycodone to balance analgesia and sedation. He briefly considered discontinuing dialysis but ultimately chose to continue. His atrial fibrillation was managed with increased diltiazem after an episode of rapid ventricular rate, and insulin was adjusted due to hypoglycemia from poor intake. He was discharged to extended care with stable vital signs, improved mental status, and clear instructions on weight monitoring and medication safety.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ PMHx ESRD on HD (___), T2DM, AFib, 
Hep C, left brachiocephalic AV fistula with steal syndrome s/p 
ligation, now presenting with weakness and altered mental 
status.  
 
ACTIVE ISSUES:

# TOXIC METABOLIC ENCEPHALOPATHY, CAUSING ALTERED MENTAL STATUS: 
The patient presented with confusion, in the setting of 
incomplete hemodialysis session the day prior, excess narcotics 
for chronic pain, as well as supratherapeutic digoxin level. He 
received HD while in house, narcotics were held, as was digoxin 
until his digoxin level reached therapeutic range. High-dose 
APAP and lidocaine patches were used for analgesia, as well as 
low-dose oxycodone to good effect. His mental status changes had 
cleared. 
 
# END-STAGE RENAL DISEASE: His incompelte HD session the day 
prior to presentation likely contributed to his altered mental 
status, as well as narcotics, as above. In house, the patient 
received hemodialysis on ___ to good effect. Midodrine, prior 
to HD, sevelamer, NephroCaps as well as renal diet supplemented 
by Nepro was continued while in house. 
 
  ## HYPERPARATHYROIDISM: While in house, the patient was 
observed to have hypercalcemia. PTH level was checked and was 
156. Vitamin D level was pending at the time of discharge. This 
is consistent with hyperparathyroidism, either secondary or 
tertiary. The patient was restarted on cinacalcet at the time of 
discharge. 

# DEPRESSION: The patient carries a diagnosis of MDD. While in 
house, he was observed to have flattened affect and sadness. He 
reported being sad and going through a difficult time, as during 
his hospitalization was the ___ year anniversary of his brother's 
death. He is on citalopram and mirtazapine for depression, as 
well as nortriptylline for pain. He was not actively or 
passively suicidal while in house. Social work visits were 
repeatedly offered, however the patient declined. 

# L SHOULDER PAIN: will manage pain per above, avoiding sedating 
medications. Unclear how much pain the patient is actually 
having, as he gives variable responses to questioning and 
appears to be resting comfortably. Shoulder XR as outpatient on 
___ demonstrated unchanged DJD, without fracture. 
Palliative care was consulted while in house to make 
recommendations about further management of the patient's pain. 
The recommended continuing the current regimen with OxyContin 10 
mg once daily in the AM with oxycodone 2.5-5 mg q4-6 hours for 
pain, as well as APAP 1 g tid and lidocaine patches. They plan 
to follow up with the patient as an outpatient. 
 
# HYPERKALEMIA: Likely secondary to incomplete hemodialysis 
session on ___. Elevated to 6, without EKG changes 
appreciated. Resolved with hemodialysis. 

# ATRIAL FIBRILLATION/ATRIAL FLUTTER, S/P ABLATION (___): The 
patient has a h/o atrial tachycardia, s/p EPS ___ and ablation 
x 2, but is not on coumadin due to history of GIBs. While 
asymptomatic, the patient was observed to enter atrial flutter, 
with variable conduction block, up to 6:1, as well as atrial 
flutter, with heart rates in the 40-50s range. This was likely 
in the setting of electrolyte abnormalities and supratherapeutic 
digoxin level (in the setting of receiving this medication 
daily, as opposed to every other day, while at rehab). At 
discharge, digoxin level was 2.0. Plan to restart digoxin at 
original home dosing, qod, on the day following discharge. 
Continued home diltiazem in divided dosing while in house, with 
resumption of XL dosing on discharge. 

# SUPRATHERAPEUTIC DIGOXIN LEVEL: Digoxin level noted to be 2.7 
upon admission, and unchanged on repeat check. Likely elevated 
given patient report of receiving daily at ___, as opposed to 
every other day. Digoxin held in house. On discharge, level was 
2.0. Planned to restart dosing, as qod, on the day after 
discharge.

INACTIVE ISSUES.
# DIABETES MELLITUS, TYPE 2, C/B PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY
- Continued home Lantus and insulin SS
- Continued renal dosing of gabapentin
 
# CAD: History of demand ischemia in ___ with no 
flow-limiting stenoses on cardiac catheterization. MIBI in 
___ showed reversible defects inferior/lateral. Baseline 
troponin 0.4-0.7. Cath in ___ - normal coronaries.  
- Will f/u with cardiology as an outpatient per PCP  
 
#SYSTOLIC CHF: EF 30% ___ TTE): Currently on digoxin. No 
signs of CHF exacerbation at this time.  
- Held digoxin for now per above. 
 
# HYPERTENSION: on diltiazem per above   
# DYSLIPIDEMIA: Not currently on a statin, as allergic to 
Lipitor  
# GERD: continue omeprazole   
# DEPRESSION: On citalopram, as well as mirtazapine, and 
nortriptylline for chronic pain. 
- Continue home citalopram, hold mirtazapine for now to avoid 
sedation 

*** TRANSITIONAL ISSUES ***
- ENSURE DOSING OF DIGOXIN Q.O.D. AND *NOT* QD
- AVOID INCREASING NARCOTICS WITHOUT TOUCHING BASE WITH 
PCP/PALLIATIVE CARE
- NO FLEET ENEMAS, GIVEN CALCIUM & PHOSPHATE LOAD IN RENAL 
DISEASE
